    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [31:0] a,
    input [31:0] b,

<module id="multi_8bit">
    <description>8-bit multiplier using shift-and-add method.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[7:0]">First 8-bit input operand (multiplicand).</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[7:0]">Second 8-bit input operand (multiplier).</input>
        <output id="product" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit output representing the product of A and B.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Initialize product to 0
        product = 16'b0;
        
        // Iterate over each bit of the multiplier B
        for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) {
            // If the current bit of B is 1, add the multiplicand A shifted left by i positions to the product
            if (B[i] == 1'b1) {
                product = product + (A << i);
            }
        }
    </implementation>
</module>

        <reg id="data_out_reg" width_description="[15:0]" type="register">Register to store the 16-bit output data.</reg>
        <reg id="flag" type="register">Flag to indicate if the first valid data has been received.</reg>
        <wire id="next_flag" type="wire">Next value of the flag.</wire>

        <register id="areg" width="16">Multiplicand register.</register>
        <register id="breg" width="16">Multiplier register.</register>
        <register id="yout_r" width="32">Product register.</register>
        <register id="done_r" width="1">Completion flag register.</register>

        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

                    done_r <= 1'b1;
                end else begin

<module id="edge_detect">
    <description>Detects rising and falling edges in the input signal a and generates corresponding output signals rise and down.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="a">Input signal.</input>
        <output id="rise">Output signal indicating a rising edge.</output>
        <output id="down">Output signal indicating a falling edge.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter>RISING</parameter>
        <parameter>FALLING</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="a_prev" width_description="1">Previous value of input signal a.</reg>
        <reg id="rise_reg" width_description="1">Register for storing the rising edge signal.</reg>
        <reg id="down_reg" width_description="1">Register for storing the falling edge signal.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                a_prev <= 0;
                rise_reg <= 0;
                down_reg <= 0;
            end else begin
                a_prev <= a;
                if (a_prev == 0 && a == 1) begin
                    rise_reg <= 1;
                    down_reg <= 0;
                end else if (a_prev == 1 && a == 0) begin
                    rise_reg <= 0;
                    down_reg <= 1;
                end else begin
                    rise_reg <= 0;
                    down_reg <= 0;
                end
            end
        end
        assign rise = rise_reg;
        assign down = down_reg;
    </implementation>
</module>

    <description>Generates a triangle wave signal by incrementing and decrementing a 5-bit signal named 'wave'.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <output id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">5-bit output waveform signal representing the generated waveform.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE">0</parameter>
        <parameter name="INCREMENT">1</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        reg [4:0] wave;
        reg [1:0] state;

        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                wave <= 5'b00000;
                state <= IDLE;
            end else begin
                case (state)
                    IDLE: begin
                        wave <= wave + 1;
                        if (wave == 5'b11111) begin
                            state <= INCREMENT;
                        end
                    end
                    INCREMENT: begin
                        wave <= wave - 1;
                        if (wave == 5'b00000) begin
                            state <= IDLE;
                        end
                    end
                    default: begin
                        // Default state should not occur
                        wave <= 5'b00000;
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Generates a triangle wave by incrementing and decrementing a 5-bit signal.</implementation>

    <description>Accumulates 4 input 8-bit data values and outputs their sum.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock input for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input data for addition.</input>

        <output id="valid_out">Output signal indicating when 4 input data accumulation is reached.</output>
        <output id="data_out" width_description="[9:0]">10-bit output data representing the accumulated sum.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="ACCUMULATE_COUNT">4</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="count" width="2">Count of valid input data received.</reg>
        <reg id="accumulated_sum" width="10">Sum of accumulated data.</reg>
        <wire id="new_data_valid">Indicates if new data is valid.</wire>

    <description>Frequency divider for generating 50MHz, 10MHz, and 1MHz clocks from a 100MHz input clock.</description>

        <input id="CLK_in">Input clock signal.</input>

        <parameter id="DIV_1">1</parameter>
    </parameter_description>

        <reg id="cnt_50" type="sequential_logic">Counter for generating 50MHz clock.</reg>
        <reg id="cnt_10" type="sequential_logic">Counter for generating 10MHz clock.</reg>

                cnt_10 <= 0;
                cnt_100 <= 0;

                CLK_10_out <= 0;
                CLK_1_out <= 0;

                cnt_50 <= cnt_50 + 1;

        end

<module id="synchronizer">
    <description>A multi-bit MUX-based synchronizer that ensures data remains constant during data_en high periods and synchronizes it across two clocks.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk_a" width_description="">Clock signal A used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="clk_b" width_description="">Clock signal B used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="arstn" width_description="">Active-low reset signal A. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="brstn" width_description="">Active-low reset signal B. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[3:0]">Input data signal of size 4 bits.</input>
        <input id="data_en" width_description="">Input enable signal that controls the selection operation.</input>
        <output id="dataout" width_description="[3:0]">Output data signal of size 4 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description></parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="data_reg" width_description="[3:0]" type="register">Register to store the input data signal.</reg>
        <reg id="en_data_reg" width_description="" type="register">Register to store the input enable signal.</reg>
        <reg id="en_clap_one" width_description="" type="register">First enable control register.</reg>
        <reg id="en_clap_two" width_description="" type="register">Second enable control register.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Data Register Update
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (!arstn) begin
                data_reg <= 4'b0;
            end else begin
                if (data_en) begin
                    data_reg <= data_in;
                end
            end
        end

        // Enable Data Register Update
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (!arstn) begin
                en_data_reg <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                en_data_reg <= data_en;
            end
        end

        // Enable Control Registers Update
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (!brstn) begin
                en_clap_one <= 1'b0;
                en_clap_two <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                en_clap_one <= en_data_reg;
                en_clap_two <= en_clap_one;
            end
        end

        // Output Assignment
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (!brstn) begin
                dataout <= 4'b0;
            end else begin
                if (en_clap_two) begin
                    dataout <= data_reg;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="parallel2serial">
    <description>Parallel-to-serial converter where every four input bits are converted to a serial one bit output (MSB to LSB).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel data input.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal indicating the availability of serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="DATA_WIDTH">4</parameter>
        <parameter name="SERIAL_WIDTH">1</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width="2">Counter register.</reg>
        <reg id="data" width="4">Data register.</reg>
        <wire id="valid">Internal valid signal.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 2'b00;
                data <= 4'b0000;
                valid <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt == 2'b11) begin
                    data <= d;
                    cnt <= 2'b00;
                    valid <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    cnt <= cnt + 1'b1;
                    valid <= 1'b0;
                    data <= {data[2:0], d[cnt]};
                end
            end
        end
        assign dout = data[3];
        assign valid_out = valid;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="div_8bit">
    <description>Implement a simplified radix-2 divider on 8-bit signed or unsigned integers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst">The reset signal to initialize or reset the module.</input>
        <input id="sign">1-bit indicates if the operation is signed (1) or unsigned (0).</input>
        <input id="dividend" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input signal representing the dividend for division.</input>
        <input id="divisor" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input signal representing the divisor for division.</input>
        <input id="opn_valid">1-bit indicates that a valid operation request is present.</input>
        <input id="res_ready">1-bit indicates that the 16-bit output result has already been acknowledged.</input>
        <output id="res_valid">1-bit output signal indicating the result is valid and ready.</output>
        <output id="result" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit the output containing the remainder in the upper 8 bits and the quotient in the lower 8 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE"/>
        <parameter name="LOAD"/>
        <parameter name="DIVIDE"/>
        <parameter name="STORE"/>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="SR" width="9"/> <!-- Shift Register -->
        <reg id="NEG_DIVISOR" width="9"/> <!-- Negated Divisor -->
        <reg id="cnt" width="4"/> <!-- Counter -->
        <reg id="start_cnt" width="1"/> <!-- Start Counter Flag -->
        <reg id="quotient" width="8"/> <!-- Quotient -->
        <reg id="remainder" width="8"/> <!-- Remainder -->
        <reg id="abs_dividend" width="8"/> <!-- Absolute Value of Dividend -->
        <reg id="abs_divisor" width="8"/> <!-- Absolute Value of Divisor -->
        <reg id="carry_out" width="1"/> <!-- Carry Out from Subtraction -->
        <reg id="temp_result" width="9"/> <!-- Temporary Result for Multiplexer -->
        <reg id="current_state" width="3"/> <!-- Current State of FSM -->
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
            if (rst) begin
                current_state <= IDLE;
                SR <= 0;
                NEG_DIVISOR <= 0;
                cnt <= 0;
                start_cnt <= 0;
                quotient <= 0;
                remainder <= 0;
                abs_dividend <= 0;
                abs_divisor <= 0;
                carry_out <= 0;
                temp_result <= 0;
                res_valid <= 0;
                result <= 0;
            end else begin
                case (current_state)
                    IDLE: begin
                        if (opn_valid && !res_valid) begin
                            current_state <= LOAD;
                            abs_dividend <= (sign == 1'b1) ? ~dividend + 1 : dividend;
                            abs_divisor <= (sign == 1'b1) ? ~divisor + 1 : divisor;
                            SR <= {abs_dividend, 1'b0};
                            NEG_DIVISOR <= {abs_divisor, 1'b0};
                            cnt <= 1;
                            start_cnt <= 1;
                            quotient <= 0;
                            remainder <= 0;
                        end else begin
                            current_state <= IDLE;
                        end
                    end
                    LOAD: begin
                        current_state <= DIVIDE;
                    end
                    DIVIDE: begin
                        if (cnt == 8) begin
                            current_state <= STORE;
                        end else begin
                            temp_result = SR - NEG_DIVISOR;
                            carry_out = temp_result[8];
                            SR <= {temp_result[7:0], carry_out};
                            quotient <= {quotient[6:0], carry_out};
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    STORE: begin
                        remainder <= SR[7:0];
                        quotient <= {quotient[6:0], SR[8]};
                        current_state <= IDLE;
                    end
                endcase

                if (rst) begin
                    res_valid <= 0;
                end else begin
                    if (cnt == 8) begin
                        res_valid <= 1;
                    end else if (res_valid && res_ready) begin
                        res_valid <= 0;
                    end
                end

                result <= {remainder, quotient};
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="adder_pipe_64bit">
    <description>64-bit ripple carry adder with pipelining stages.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock input.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="i_en">Enable signal for addition operation.</input>
        <input id="adda" width_description="[63:0]">64-bit input operand A.</input>
        <input id="addb" width_description="[63:0]">64-bit input operand B.</input>
        <output id="result" width_description="[64:0]">65-bit output representing the sum of adda and addb.</output>
        <output id="o_en">Output enable signal indicating the availability of the result.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE">Idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter name="ADD">Addition state.</parameter>
        <parameter name="RESULT">Result state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="current_state" width="2">Current state of the FSM.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" width="2">Next state of the FSM.</reg>
        <reg id="enable_reg" width="1">Register to hold the enable signal.</reg>
        <reg id="adda_reg" width_description="[63:0]">Register to hold the first input operand.</reg>
        <reg id="addb_reg" width_description="[63:0]">Register to hold the second input operand.</reg>
        <reg id="carry_out_reg" width="1">Register to hold the carry out signal.</reg>
        <wire id="sum" width_description="[63:0]">Sum of adda and addb.</wire>
        <wire id="carry_in" width="1">Carry in signal for the next stage.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // State transition logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                current_state <= IDLE;
            end else begin
                current_state <= next_state;
            end
        end

        always @(*) begin
            case (current_state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (i_en) begin
                        next_state = ADD;
                        enable_reg = 1;
                        adda_reg = adda;
                        addb_reg = addb;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = IDLE;
                        enable_reg = 0;
                    end
                end
                ADD: begin
                    next_state = RESULT;
                    sum = adda_reg + addb_reg + carry_out_reg;
                    carry_in = sum[63];
                end
                RESULT: begin
                    next_state = IDLE;
                    carry_out_reg = carry_in;
                end
                default: begin
                    next_state = IDLE;
                end
            endcase
        end

        // Output logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                o_en <= 0;
                result <= 65'b0;
            end else begin
                if (current_state == RESULT && enable_reg) begin
                    o_en <= 1;
                    result <= {carry_out_reg, sum};
                end else begin
                    o_en <= 0;
                    result <= 65'b0;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="pulse_detect">
    <description>Pulse detection module. Detects a pulse when data_in transitions from 0 to 1 to 0 (3 cycles). Outputs data_out as 1 at the end cycle of the pulse.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="data_in">One-bit input signal.</input>
        <output id="data_out">Output signal indicating the presence of pulses.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE">Idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter name="RISING">Rising edge detected.</parameter>
        <parameter name="FALLING">Falling edge detected.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="state" type="reg" width="2">State register.</register>
        <wire id="next_state" type="wire" width="2">Next state wire.</wire>
        <wire id="data_out_reg" type="wire">Data_out register.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                state <= IDLE;
                data_out_reg <= 0;
            end else begin
                case (state)
                    IDLE: begin
                        if (data_in == 1'b1) begin
                            next_state = RISING;
                        end else begin
                            next_state = IDLE;
                        end
                        data_out_reg = 0;
                    end
                    RISING: begin
                        if (data_in == 1'b0) begin
                            next_state = FALLING;
                        end else begin
                            next_state = RISING;
                        end
                        data_out_reg = 0;
                    end
                    FALLING: begin
                        if (data_in == 1'b1) begin
                            next_state = IDLE;
                        end else begin
                            next_state = FALLING;
                        end
                        data_out_reg = 1;
                    end
                    default: begin
                        next_state = IDLE;
                        data_out_reg = 0;
                    end
                endcase
                state <= next_state;
                data_out <= data_out_reg;
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_pipe_4bit">
    <description>4-bit unsigned number pipeline multiplier with two levels of registers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit input signal representing the multiplicand.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit input signal representing the multiplier.</input>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit product output signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <param name="size">4</param>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="partial_products" width_description="[3:0][3:0]">Array to store partial products.</reg>
        <reg id="intermediate_sum" width_description="[7:0]">Register to store intermediate sum.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Extend input signals by adding 'size' number of zero bits at the most significant bit positions
        reg [7:0] mul_a_extended;
        reg [7:0] mul_b_extended;
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_a_extended <= 8'd0;
                mul_b_extended <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                mul_a_extended <= {mul_a, 4'b0};
                mul_b_extended <= {mul_b, 4'b0};
            end
        end

        // Generate partial products
        genvar i;
        generate
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin : partial_product_gen
                always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
                    if (!rst_n) begin
                        partial_products[i] <= 4'b0;
                    end else begin
                        if (mul_b_extended[i]) begin
                            partial_products[i] <= mul_a_extended << i;
                        end else begin
                            partial_products[i] <= 4'b0;
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        endgenerate

        // Add partial products to get the intermediate sum
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                intermediate_sum <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                intermediate_sum <= partial_products[0] + partial_products[1] + partial_products[2] + partial_products[3];
            end
        end

        // Assign the final product to the output
        assign mul_out = intermediate_sum;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Unsigned 8-bit multiplier implemented using pipelining.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. 0 for reset, 1 for normal operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal controlling the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplicand input with 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplier input with 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output with 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description></parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic"></logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Pipeline stages
        reg [7:0] mul_a_reg;
        reg [7:0] mul_b_reg;
        reg [7:0] temp [0:7];
        reg [15:0] sum [0:7];
        reg [15:0] mul_out_reg;
        reg mul_en_out_reg;

        // Pipeline control
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_a_reg <= 8'b0;
                mul_b_reg <= 8'b0;
                mul_en_out_reg <= 1'b0;
                mul_out_reg <= 16'b0;
                for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) begin
                    temp[i] <= 8'b0;
                    sum[i] <= 16'b0;
                end
            end else begin
                if (mul_en_in) begin
                    mul_a_reg <= mul_a;
                    mul_b_reg <= mul_b;
                    mul_en_out_reg <= mul_en_in;
                end

                // Partial product generation
                for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) begin
                    temp[i] <= mul_a_reg & (mul_b_reg >>> i);
                end

                // Partial sum calculation
                for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) begin
                    sum[i] <= sum[i-1] + temp[i];
                end

                // Final product calculation
                mul_out_reg <= sum[7];
            end
        end

        // Output assignment
        assign mul_en_out = mul_en_out_reg;
        assign mul_out = mul_out_reg;
    </implementation>
</module>

        <reg type="sequential_logic" id="state" width="2">Current state of the traffic light controller.</reg>
        <reg type="sequential_logic" id="p_red" width="1">Previous red signal.</reg>

        <reg type="sequential_logic" id="p_green" width="1">Previous green signal.</reg>
    </logic_description>

                p_green <= 1'b0;

                        yellow <= 1'b0;

                        yellow <= 1'b0;

<module id="asyn_fifo">
    <description>Asynchronous FIFO with configurable depth and width.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="wclk">Write clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rclk">Read clock signal.</input>
        <input id="wrstn">Write reset signal.</input>
        <input id="rrstn">Read reset signal.</input>
        <input id="winc">Write increment signal.</input>
        <input id="rinc">Read increment signal.</input>
        <input id="wdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Write data input.</input>
        <output id="wfull">Write full signal.</output>
        <output id="rempty">Read empty signal.</output>
        <output id="rdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Read data output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="waddr_bin" width_description="$clog2(DEPTH)">Write address register.</register>
        <register id="raddr_bin" width_description="$clog2(DEPTH)">Read address register.</register>
        <register id="wptr" width_description="$clog2(DEPTH)">Write pointer register.</register>
        <register id="rptr" width_description="$clog2(DEPTH)">Read pointer register.</register>
        <register id="wptr_buff" width_description="$clog2(DEPTH)">Write pointer buffer.</register>
        <register id="rptr_buff" width_description="$clog2(DEPTH)">Read pointer buffer.</register>
        <wire id="wen" width_description="1">Write enable signal.</wire>
        <wire id="ren" width_description="1">Read enable signal.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Dual-port RAM instantiation
        <submodule id="dual_port_RAM">
            <port id="wclk">Write clock signal.</port>
            <port id="renc">Read enable signal.</port>
            <port id="waddr">Write address.</port>
            <port id="wdata">Write data.</port>
            <port id="rclk">Read clock signal.</port>
            <port id="wenc">Write enable signal.</port>
            <port id="raddr">Read address.</port>
            <port id="rdata">Read data.</port>
        </submodule>

        // Write pointer management
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                waddr_bin <= 0;
            end else if (winc && !wfull) begin
                waddr_bin <= waddr_bin + 1;
            end
        end

        // Read pointer management
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                raddr_bin <= 0;
            end else if (rinc && !rempty) begin
                raddr_bin <= raddr_bin + 1;
            end
        end

        // Gray code conversion
        assign wptr = waddr_bin ^ (waddr_bin >> 1);
        assign rptr = raddr_bin ^ (raddr_bin >> 1);

        // Pointer buffers
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                wptr_buff <= 0;
            end else begin
                wptr_buff <= wptr;
            end
        end

        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                rptr_buff <= 0;
            end else begin
                rptr_buff <= rptr;
            end
        end

        // Full and empty signals
        assign wfull = (wptr == {~rptr[most_significant_bit(rptr)], rptr[$clog2(DEPTH)-2:0]});
        assign rempty = (rptr == wptr);

        // Data write controller
        assign wen = winc && !wfull;

        // Data read controller
        assign ren = rinc && !rempty;

        // Connect to dual-port RAM
        dual_port_RAM.wclk <= wclk;
        dual_port_RAM.renc <= ren;
        dual_port_RAM.waddr <= wptr;
        dual_port_RAM.wdata <= wdata;
        dual_port_RAM.rclk <= rclk;
        dual_port_RAM.wenc <= wen;
        dual_port_RAM.raddr <= rptr;
        rdata <= dual_port_RAM.rdata;
    </implementation>
</module>
